items.action: Rename `buttonRef()` to `controlRef()` on every ds-button template reference, and narrow `.nativeElement` yourself where you read a button-only property off it.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that reads the reference — a template ref used to position or refocus an overlay, or a component that calls it. Nothing changes for a consumer who only uses the element and its inputs, and the property behind the name is the same view child.
items.pitfall: The rename is a compile error and announces itself; the type change may not. `.nativeElement.disabled`, `.form` and `.type` were reachable on `HTMLButtonElement` and are gone from `HTMLElement`, so a read of one fails to compile — but a cast written to silence it then lies at runtime whenever the button carries a destination and really is an anchor.
items.note: The element ds-button renders now follows its destination: an `<a>` when `routerLink` or `href` is set, the `<button>` otherwise. One name and one type had to cover all three, so both were wrong before. Overlay triggers pass `.nativeElement` for positioning and focus, which `HTMLElement` answers.
items.verify: No `buttonRef` remains anywhere in the consumer tree, and every read of `controlRef().nativeElement` either uses only HTMLElement members or narrows with an `instanceof HTMLButtonElement` check.

items.action: Build after upgrading, then rename or mark `override` any member the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends ButtonComponent. A consumer who uses the element in a template needs nothing from this item.
items.pitfall: Two of the four are not public API, which is no protection: a redeclared private or protected member fails with TS2415 exactly as a public collision does, and a same-named method whose signature differs fails with TS2416 instead.
items.note: ButtonComponent gained `routerLink` and `href`, the two destination inputs; `controlRef`, the view child that replaces `buttonRef`; and `destination`, the computed that decides which of the three elements renders. It also LOST `buttonRef`, so a subclass that overrode that one now overrides nothing and its member is dead rather than broken.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS2416 naming ButtonComponent, and no member of your subclass is called routerLink, href, controlRef or destination.

informational: `ds-button` takes two new optional inputs, `routerLink` and `href`. Unset, which is the default and what every existing button has, it renders the same `<button type="button">` as before. Set either and it renders an `<a>` instead, with identical styling — the rules are class-based, so nothing keyed to `.button` moves. `type` and `loading` are ignored on a link and say so in dev mode.

A `ds-multi-select` panel filter row now carries `--ds-radius-inner`, so its focus ring is rounded instead of a full-width rectangle. Nothing to change — an `outline` follows the radius of the box it is drawn on, and that row simply had none.

A focus ring is now shaped by its host: the new `--focus-ring-radius` token gives a box that exists only to carry the ring a radius, because an outline follows the `border-radius` of the box it is drawn on and has none of its own. It follows `--ds-radius-inner`, 4px, so a theme that retunes the inner radius moves these rings with it. `ds-checkbox`, `ds-radio` and `ds-switch` pick it up, so their keyboard focus ring is rounded instead of square. Nothing to change — the resting state of all three is untouched, and a host with its own radius keeps it.

A clickable `ds-table` row, a `ds-tree` row and a `ds-list` activator now carry `--focus-ring-radius`, so their keyboard focus ring is rounded instead of square. Nothing to change: none of the three paints a background of its own, so the radius shapes only the ring, and their resting appearance is unchanged.

A field marked `disabled` no longer paints its `data-field-state`. An `error`, `warning` or `success` state used to out-rank the disabled look in `ds-input`, `ds-textarea`, `ds-select`, `ds-multi-select`, `ds-autocomplete`, `ds-date-picker`, `ds-time-picker`, `ds-color-picker` and `ds-otp-input`, on specificity alone, so a field left invalid and then disabled kept a red border and fill it could not act on. Nothing to change — `data-field-state` is set the same way and means the same thing, and a read-only field still paints it, because `readonly` is submitted where `disabled` is not.
